name: obs-studio
summary: Desktop broadcasting and recording suite for scene automation, streaming, and capture workflows.
why_it_matters: OBS Studio preserves meaningful media-production capability knowledge, but desktop, plugin, and GPU complexity make it better treated as a blueprint until a scenario proves the support model.
when_to_use: A future scenario needs automated recording or live-stream composition.
Operators want programmable scene switching and capture orchestration.
The workflow depends on obs-websocket or desktop capture features.

platform_support.notes: OBS is cross-platform, but capture permissions, plugins, and GPU/desktop behavior differ substantially across host environments.

implementation_notes: Promotion should validate a real scene automation workflow instead of generic app lifecycle control.
Keep desktop capture support separate from streaming destination support.
Plugin expectations should be explicit and version-pinned.
operational_notes: GPU and capture permission issues are the main support burden.
Health checks should verify websocket automation if that is the intended contract.
Desktop apps require stronger environment assumptions than containerized services.
risks: Desktop media automation is operationally brittle across hosts.
A shallow wrapper would imply more reliability than exists.
